author: Boddaert, 1783
summary: 전국에 찾아오는 비교적 드문 여름철새로, 혼자 또는 암수가 함께 지낸다. 하천가나 산 중턱 벼랑에 구멍을 파거나 나무 구멍을 써서 4~7월에 알을 4~6개 낳는다. 갑각류, 파충류, 양서류, 물고기, 곤충 따위를 먹는다. 국외에서는 중국, 인도, 스리랑카에 분포한다.

art.subject: Black-capped Kingfisher (Halcyon pileata), adult (sexes similar), as seen along Korean rivers in summer: whole head jet-black down to below the eye, sharply cut off from the white throat; broad white collar around the neck; chin, throat and upper breast white to buffy white; lower breast, belly, flanks and undertail rich orange-rufous; wing coverts black, forming a black shoulder; mantle, back, rump, outer edges of the flight feathers and tail deep glossy violet-blue. Bill very large, straight and dagger-like, bright coral-red; dark eye; legs and feet red.
art.pose: perched alone on a branch above a stream
art.scene: Korean riverside in summer with an earthen bank and a hillside cliff; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched: jet-black head, white collar and throat, buffy-white breast, orange-rufous belly, black shoulder, glossy violet-blue back, wings and tail, huge coral-red bill, red feet
adult in flight, seen from above: violet-blue back and tail, black wing coverts, large white patches at the base of the primaries
art.build: Large kingfisher, about 28cm, about the length of a Brown-eared Bulbul but much stockier, big-headed and short-tailed; perches upright. Bill massive, longer than the head, straight on the ridge with the lower edge slightly angled, thick at the base and pointed. Legs very short, red. Tail medium-length and square-ended. In flight a large white patch at the base of the primaries shows on each wing, contrasting with the black coverts and blue flight feathers.
avoid: Do not paint a black or dark bill; the bill is bright coral-red.
Do not paint a chestnut-brown head and belly with a white bib; that is White-throated Kingfisher (Halcyon smyrnensis).
Do not paint all-rufous plumage (Ruddy Kingfisher, Halcyon coromanda) or the small turquoise Common Kingfisher.
Do not paint blue wing coverts or a white belly; the coverts are black and the belly orange-rufous.
